summary: In this episode, Fathers Andrew Stephen Damick and Stephen De Young explore how the first disciples recognized Jesus as the Messiah, not primarily through fulfilled prophecies but through their direct encounters with Him. They argue that Jesus embodied Israel, the Torah, and the God of Israel, which led people to identify Him as the Christ. The discussion emphasizes that Jesus recapitulates Israel's history, fulfills the Torah as a way of life, and reveals the humility of God. The episode also addresses modern misunderstandings, such as the tendency to de-Judaize Christianity, and calls for a re-embrace of the Jewish heritage of the faith.

entities.title: Jesus Christ
entities.summary: The central figure of Christianity, recognized as the Messiah by His disciples through His embodiment of Israel, Torah, and God.

entities.title: Israel
entities.summary: The people of God in the Old Testament, whose history and experience Jesus embodies and recapitulates.

entities.title: Torah
entities.summary: The first five books of the Bible, understood as a way of life, not just law, which Jesus embodies and fulfills.

entities.title: God of Israel
entities.summary: The particular God revealed in the Hebrew Scriptures, characterized by humility and covenant faithfulness, embodied by Jesus.

entities.title: St. Peter
entities.summary: One of Jesus' disciples who first confessed Him as the Messiah, as recounted in the Gospels.

entities.title: St. Paul
entities.summary: Apostle who taught that Jesus embodies the Torah and that Christians walk according to the Spirit, fulfilling the Torah.

entities.title: Ezekiel
entities.summary: Old Testament prophet whose vision of the dry bones symbolizes the death and resurrection of Israel, which Jesus embodies.

concepts.title: Jesus Embodies Israel
concepts.summary: Jesus recapitulates the history and experience of Israel, succeeding where Israel failed, and thus is recognized as the Messiah.

concepts.title: Jesus Embodies the Torah
concepts.summary: Jesus embodies the Torah as a way of life, teaching and living it perfectly, and fulfilling it by filling it full.

concepts.title: Jesus Embodies the God of Israel
concepts.summary: Jesus reveals the character of the God of Israel, particularly His humility, and embodies His relationship with His people.

concepts.title: Messiah as Identity
concepts.summary: The New Testament claim that Jesus is the Messiah is not about a checklist of fulfilled prophecies but about His identity, which is revealed through His embodiment of Israel, Torah, and God.

concepts.title: Fulfillment of Prophecy
concepts.summary: Prophecy is not a list of specific predictions but a pattern that Jesus embodies, and He fulfills all prophecies in a deeper sense.

claims.text: Jesus embodies Israel, succeeding where Israel failed, and thus is recognized as the Messiah.
Jesus fulfills the Torah not by abolishing it but by embodying it as a way of life, filling it full.
Jesus reveals the humility of God, who identifies with the weak and powerless, as seen throughout the Old Testament.
Old Testament prophecy is not a checklist of specific predictions but a pattern that Jesus embodies, and He fulfills all prophecies in a deeper sense.
Christianity is a form of Judaism, and de-Judaizing Christianity warps its true nature.

scriptural_links.summary: Quoted by Matthew to show Jesus as embodying Israel's experience of being called out of Egypt.

Jesus came not to abolish the law but to fulfill it, understood as filling it full.
